Exam Date & Time: 04-May-2024 (02:30 PM - 05:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MIT BLR - BTech VI Semester - End Semester Examination - April / May -2024  
  Big Data Analytics [CSE-3272]  
Marks: 50                                                                           Duration: 180 mins.  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
1)           With the help of a neat diagram interpret the deployment modes for Spark  
  applications running on YARN and list the YARN features.  
  (5)  
  A)  
  B)      Elaborate on the structured streaming Data Sinks, File Sink and Memory Sink with  
  syntax.                                                                                 (3)  
  
  C)      Write code snippets to demonstrate the use of map() and filter() transformations on  
  the data to achieve specific transformations. Interpret the expected output for each    (2)  
  code snippet.  
  
2)           Analyse and illustrate the Alternating Least Squares Recommender Algorithm.  
  Explore the trade-offs between recommendation accuracy and efficiency. How can  
  (5)  
  you optimize the system to balance these factors for a specific application?  
  A)  
  B)      Interpret the concept of Resilient Distributed Datasets (RDDs) in Spark. How do they  
  contribute to fault tolerance?                                                       (3)  
  
  C)      Interpret the significance of the ROC curve in model performance estimation.            (2)  
3)           Elaborate on the steps involved in the construction and evaluation of a decision tree  
  model for personalized product recommendations, leveraging the power of Spark to  
  (5)  
  handle large-scale e-commerce data with code snippets.  
  A)  
  B)      Interpret the role of Spark drivers and executors in running Spark applications. How  
  does Spark handle task scheduling and fault tolerance during job execution?          (3)  
  
  C)      Analyze how you'll use GraphX's Vertex and Edge classes to represent nodes and  
  relationships within your chosen network.                                               (2)  
  
4)           Analyze the steps for building and analyzing a co-occurrence network in the  
  MEDLINE Citation Index dataset using GraphX.  
  (5)  
  A)  
  B)      Demonstrate how the trade-off between bias and variance changes as the depth  
  increases when tuning the maximum depth of a decision tree.                             (3)  
  
  C)      Use the appropriate syntax and example to demonstrate the following  
  transformations, keys() and values() in RDD.                                            (2)  
  
5)           Evaluate the key steps involved in conducting a Monte Carlo simulation With             (5)

appropriate examples.  
  
  A)  
  B)          Interpret the common applications of Monte Carlo simulation in big data analytics.   (3)  
  C)          Relate and explain the significance of socketTextStream() API with syntax and  
  examples.                                                                            (2)  
  
  
-----End-----
